title: Threat Lock
definition: Chronic activation of Protection, Control, or Domination where the system becomes stuck in defense without return to Connection.
summary: When pattern hijack occurs repeatedly without resolution, the nervous system can become locked in defensive mode. The baseline shifts toward chronic protection. Connection becomes difficult to access, and the system operates as if threat is continuous even when the environment is objectively safe.

content.title: What It Is
content.content: Threat lock occurs when the nervous system becomes chronically stuck outside Connection. The mechanism: (1) repeated activation without return to baseline, (2) system 'learns' that protection is continuously needed, (3) baseline shifts toward chronic defense, (4) Connection becomes difficult or impossible to access. Characteristics include persistent hypervigilance or numbness, inability to relax even in safe environments, and relationships feeling exhausting or threatening.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Maps It
content.content: TEG-Blue distinguishes between temporary Protection (adaptive response to real threat) and threat lock (chronic defensive state). Threat lock can manifest as stuck Protection (hypervigilance, anxiety), Control (managing threat by controlling others), or Domination (power as the only safety strategy). The key variable is not which state, but whether the system can return to Connection. Treatment requires sustained safety provision, not correction or challenge.

content.title: Research Basis
content.content: Integrates concepts from complex PTSD research (Herman, van der Kolk), chronic stress literature, and polyvagal theory's concept of faulty neuroception. Threat lock is not 'personality disorder' — it is chronic defensive activation that developed for survival reasons and can be resolved through corrective relational experience.
